releaseNote.summary: Adds attributes.rowSecurity: deny-by-default row rules for the instance list and GET. Breaking: a flow lookup error now fails list and GET of every flow (D5).

rowSecurity.description: A flow declares attributes.rowSecurity.rules (role-keyed row filters in the list-engine filter language, with $.context.Headers / QueryParameters / CurrentUser parameters and the $InstanceStarter / $InstanceBehalfOfStarter identity rules). There is no default: a flow with rowSecurity is deny by default, and 'role X sees everything' is an explicit unfiltered rule; a flow without it is not filtered. A caller sees the OR of the matched static rules' filters plus declared identity rules, ANDed with their own filter; a failed role resolution or any failed parameter yields no rows from that rule and never widens. The rule set is the flow's default version (sys-version-registry pointer) when set, else the latest, read with GetFlowAsync(domain, workflow, null) for instances of every version. Behaviour change for EVERY flow, opted in or not (council decision D5, requester-approved 2026-10-23): GET now always performs a (cached) flow-definition lookup, and a lookup failure other than 'no definition' (for example Instance:100052 409 invalid default-version pointer, Instance:100053 503 version registry unavailable, flow version not activated) now fails the list and the single GET of that flow and returns the lookup error as is; before, the list ignored that error and served rows and GET did not look the flow up. Phase 1 filters only the instance list (including groupBy and aggregations) and the single GET (excluded answers the same 404 as missing, before the ETag); state/data/view/schema/master/history/internal functions and the GetInstanceData task are unfiltered, so the GET 404 is not a confidentiality boundary. Requires a gateway that strips or overwrites the role header and every header a rule reads; QueryParameters are client-controlled. Publish warnings (RS-W*) are log-only. A runtime older than this release ignores rowSecurity entirely and serves every row, whatever the flow declares; removing rowSecurity or closing the flow with an unheld role protects nothing there. The only protections are not rolling back below this release, or blocking/authorizing the list and GET of those flows at the gateway while an older runtime serves them. Requires the runtime version that ships this entry and a vnext-schema release containing workflow.attributes.rowSecurity.

knownIssues.title: rowSecurity filters the instance list and single GET only; the state/data/view/schema/master/history/internal functions and the GetInstanceData task serve excluded instances by id, and GET 404 next to data 200 is an existence oracle.
knownIssues.workaround: Do not treat rowSecurity as an access boundary for an instance whose id the caller knows; enforce access to those functions at the gateway (authorize) until instance-addressed coverage ships.
